newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cyclone survivors lose hope for missing.
newsitem.headline: Indian cyclone survivors lose hope for missing.

text.p: Relatives of hundreds of missing fishermen lost since a cyclone savaged India's south-east coast 11 days ago gave up hope on Monday of seeing them alive again.
"The total number of dead is 971 and 925 people are missing," an Andhra Pradesh state official told Reuters.
Most of the missing were fishermen who set sail shortly before the cyclone struck their villages in the coastal area of the Godavari river delta, a fertile crop growing region of the state.
According to local custom, they are presumed dead if they have not returned within 10 days.

The death toll crept steadily higher as more bodies were identified and registered with local revenue collectors. The total number of dead may never be verified because many bodies were swept out to sea.
The official, in the control room coordinating relief operations in Hyderabad, said the cyclone had caused more than $1.4 billion in damage to crops and property.
The state relief fund had so far released around $2.8 million to the cyclone hit area, he said.
Andhra Pradesh is reviewing compensation claims that have been pouring in, chief minister Chandrababu Naidu said on Saturday.
The next of kin of each deceased person will receive 100,000 rupees ($2,800) in compensation.
Naidu told a news conference some exaggerated claims had been made about crop loss and the number of missing persons. ($1 = 35.7 rupees)
